output.brief: The rise in cancellations is mainly caused by a fault in the Quillbook connector, not by the price rise. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices, and 58,300 invoices have been affected. About 34% of affected accounts have cancelled, against 8% of unaffected ones. Quillbook-connected accounts' churn roughly tripled whether they were repriced (2.0% to 6.2%) or price-locked Founders (1.9% to 5.9%). Accounts with no connector show almost no change (1.8% to 1.9%), whatever their seat count. The finance seat-band pattern is explained by larger accounts being more likely to use Quillbook. The failures are logged as warnings, so the health panel doesn't show them. Slow support responses probably add to the damage, but that is not shown to be causal. Recommended next steps: make the v3 fix (3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority, and contact every Quillbook account, including those that have cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on. Don't reverse the price rise, and don't start the Tallymarsh rebuild until its log has been reviewed. Confidence is high, with the Tallymarsh log unreviewed.
